subject: Post-call: obfuscation playbook & redaction kickoff
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Rogers <dana.rogers@exemplarhealth.com>
Cc: Samuel Holt <samuel.holt@exemplarhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — obfuscation playbook & next steps

Thanks again for the time this morning, Dana and Sam — good conversation. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we don't lose momentum:

- Acceptance criteria you outlined: remove/obfuscate PII from request/response logs (names, SSNs, patient identifiers), mask trace headers (Trace-ID / X-Request-ID), and provide tenant-scoped retention controls.
- Questions we agreed to answer:
  * Do we persist full request bodies in audit logs? (short answer: configurable)
  * Can you produce redacted exports for audits? (yes, via filtered export)
  * Data residency options: we can pin logging storage to region-level buckets (we discussed eu-west-1 as a target).

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
1) Share a redaction sample (YAML) showing header and body rules + an explanation of hashing vs truncation for trace IDs — attached.
2) Internal tech deep-dive: schedule 60-min security/infra session next week (please propose times).
3) Provide SOC 2 summary and basic onboarding checklist (attached).

Please reply with any missing items or additional constraints (e.g., retention windows, audit export format).

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redaction-sample.yml (text), SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Dana Rogers <dana.rogers@exemplarhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samuel Holt <samuel.holt@exemplarhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — obfuscation playbook & next steps

Thanks, Logan — helpful summary. A couple clarifying items from SecOps before we schedule the deep-dive:

1) Retention: analytics team needs raw request/response aggregates for 13 months, but PII must be removed after 90 days. Can Redwood support different retention for raw logs vs sanitized exports?
2) Trace IDs: our distributed tracing relies on a correlation token. We need to retain a mapping long enough for incident investigations but not the raw token in logs. Are you able to pseudonymize trace IDs (deterministic hashing per-tenant) and provide a reversible mapping to us under legal request (with key-wrapped access)?
3) Headers: please confirm you can redact or drop headers like Authorization, Cookie, and also mask any header named X-Trace-Id / Trace-ID. We need examples of the syntax/tooling you use to declare header redaction rules.
4) Residency: pilot must store logs in eu-west-1 and never replicate to other regions. Is there an explicit tenancy/region flag for logging buckets?

If you can answer those items in writing ahead of the tech session, that would speed our procurement screening.

Best,
Dana Rogers
Head of Security, Exemplar Health
dana.rogers@exemplarhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Dana Rogers <dana.rogers@exemplarhealth.com>, Samuel Holt <samuel.holt@exemplarhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — obfuscation playbook & next steps

Logan / Dana — jumping in with technical clarifications and an initial approach. Summary below — I'll bring the ops runbook to the scheduled deep-dive.
- Retention model: Redwood supports independent retention policies at the tenant level for three artifact classes: raw request/response payloads, structured telemetry (headers, timestamps, latencies), and redacted audit exports. You can set retention via the Console or the Policy API. Common config we use:
  * raw_payloads.retention_days = 90
  * telemetry.aggregates_retention_days = 395  (13 months ~ 395 days)
  * redacted_exports.retention_days = customer-defined
- Trace ID handling: two recommended options:
  1) Deterministic per-tenant hashing (SHA-256 with tenant salt) — keeps correlation but avoids raw tokens. Hashes are reversible only if you store the pre-image mapping in a KEK-wrapped vault (we can provide an API to export mapping under strict audit).
  2) Truncate + random suffix — non-reversible but preserves short-term correlation for live debugging.
- Header/body redaction: policy language supports header and body selectors. Examples attached in redaction-sample.yml. Inline example for headers:
  headers:
    - name: Authorization
      action: redact
    - name_regex: ^X-Trace-Id$
      action: hash
- Residency: logging storage can be pinned to a region via a deployment flag; for eu-west-1 we create a customer-specific storage bucket in that region and disable cross-region replication by default for Private and Dedicated customers. Hosted customers can request region-pinning for logging with a region addendum.
- Audit exports: we can produce line-delimited, gzipped redacted logs or structured Parquet exports with column-level masking.
Attachments included: redaction-sample.yml (policy examples) and a SOC2-summary.pdf. I'll add a short playbook to the tech session deck.
Notes for Logan: suggest 60-minute slot Tue/Wed next week (PST morning).
—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: redaction-sample.yml (text), SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)

Marissa — that is exactly the level of detail we need, thank you. A few follow-ups before we lock the tech session:

- Export format: we prefer Parquet with column-level masking for downstream analytics. Please confirm you can emit Parquet and share a sample schema.
- Timeline: our procurement and legal need the SOC2 summary plus the data-residency addendum before we invite Infra to the pilot. Can you route those to procurement@exemplarhealth.com?
If those items are in place, we'll aim for a pilot kickoff on 2026-12-01.
Regards,
Dana
